item.title: Nancy Guthrie missing case turns tense as YouTube streamers crowd her home and Jimmy Williams clashes with neighbor
item.description: Nancy Guthrie has been missing since February 1, 2026, and the FBI and local police are still searching. YouTube streamers have crowded outside her home, live streaming updates and sparking speculation. Sheriff Chris Nanos defended the family after online claims. Authorities have received thousands of tips. No arrests have been made yet.

item.title: “I’m borderline blind”: MrBeast opens up about right eye vision issue after viral X post questions his smile and demeanor
item.description: Jimmy Donaldson, known as MrBeast, said he is “borderline blind” in his right eye after X users criticized how his eyes look. He explained he must squint to see, even with contacts. The debate grew online, with support and criticism. The discussion started after claims that he reaches 1 billion monthly viewers worldwide.

item.title: What sparked the “Larry Wheels Files”? Inside the Greg Doucette and Jon Bravo controversy
item.description: The “Larry Wheels Files” began after Greg Doucette accused Larry Wheels of sending troubling messages and failing to repay $50,000. Jon Bravo later released a detailed video with more screenshots and claims. Larry has denied being in an open relationship and rejected parts of the allegations. The controversy continues across YouTube and fitness circles.

item.title: Who is Charles Bronson? Britain’s most notorious prisoner, will he finally be released after 50 years?
item.description: Charles Bronson, now legally Charles Salvador, has spent over 50 years in prison, much in solitary confinement, for violent offenses including hostage-taking. At 73, he faces his ninth parole review, with the board weighing his risk against decades of notoriety, personal transformation through art, and public fascination, famously dramatized by Tom Hardy in the 2008 film Bronson.

item.title: ‘I almost terminated him’: Why did Donald Trump say he wanted to fire US Secretary of State Marco Rubio?
item.description: President Trump playfully teased Secretary of State Marco Rubio and First Lady Melania Trump about sharing the spotlight at the inaugural Board of Peace meeting. The board, focused on the Gaza ceasefire and rebuilding, saw pledges of $7 billion from several nations, with the US contributing $10 billion. Trump praised both Rubio and Vice President Vance for their contributions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Clavicular makes New York City runway debut at Elena Velez show after Arizona arrest dismissal and looksmaxxing controversy
item.description: Braden Peters, known as Clavicular, brought his controversial looksmaxxing fame to New York City with a runway debut and major media coverage. Days after Arizona prosecutors dropped his arrest case, he walked for Elena Velez and livestreamed the chaos. From risky self-improvement methods to political comments, his rise shows how internet fame is moving into mainstream culture.

item.title: Lewis University moves classes online after ICE leases space in same building
item.description: Lewis University is moving some classes online at its Oak Brook location due to ICE's presence in the same building. The university cited concerns about potential protests and community worries, aiming to ensure a safe learning environment. This precautionary measure will be in effect from February 16th to 21st.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Someday, I won't be here': Trump says Board of Peace will oversee UN, will ensure it runs properly
item.description: America will boost the United Nations. President Donald Trump revealed plans to support the global body financially and ensure its proper functioning. This initiative is part of his peace plan for Gaza. Trump believes the UN has great potential and aims to help it achieve it. He also mentioned past successes in settling wars without UN involvement.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who’s really paying for your daily free ChatGPT use? OpenAI’s staggering costs revealed
item.description: ChatGPT’s explosive growth to nearly 900 million weekly users has transformed OpenAI into one of the fastest-scaling tech companies in histor, but at staggering cost. With annualized revenue surpassing $20 billion yet burn rates near $17 billion, the company is racing to balance subscriptions, enterprise sales, ads and a potential IPO against immense AI infrastructure demands.
item.dc:creator: TOI Tech Desk

item.title: White supremacist Nick Fuentes urges supporters to skip midterms, says he hopes Trump is impeached and the GOP ‘crashes and burns’
item.description: Voters are urged to abstain from the upcoming midterm elections. The author believes a Republican defeat is essential for national salvation. This stance stems from perceived failures and mistakes attributed to Republican leadership and policies. The hope is for a complete collapse of the Republican party, potentially paving the way for a radical shift in future elections.
